prompt: `rg-shop-prod-app` carries `cost-centre: cc-410`. A machine is created in it with no tags. What tags does the machine have?
hint: One of the four rules in the table.

choices.text: `cost-centre: cc-410`, inherited from the group
choices.why: Resources do not inherit their group's tags.

choices.text: Whatever the subscription carries
choices.why: A subscription's tags are not inherited either.

choices.text: None
choices.why: Right. Something has to copy the tag down, which is the next section.

choices.text: The group's tags, but only after a day
choices.why: No delay turns a group's tags into a resource's.

prompt: One team tags `cost-centre: CC-410` and another `cost-centre: cc-410`. What does a cost report show?
hint: Names and values follow different case rules.

choices.text: Two cost centres where there is one
choices.why: Right. The money of cc-410 splits into two rows.

choices.text: One cost centre, since Azure ignores case in tags
choices.why: It ignores case in names only. Values are case-sensitive.

choices.text: Nothing: the second tag was refused as a duplicate
choices.why: They are on different resources, and nothing compares them.

choices.text: One cost centre, after Cost Management lower-cases values
choices.why: Nothing lower-cases values on the way; spelling has to be agreed.

prompt: How many tag pairs may a single resource carry, by Microsoft's documented limit?
hint: The same limit applies to a group and a subscription.

prompt: In `pip.bicep`, why is `'cost-centre'` written in quotes while `environment` is not?
hint: Look at the character in the middle.

choices.text: Quoted keys are case-sensitive in Bicep
choices.why: Quoting has nothing to do with case.

choices.text: The cost centre is a secret and must be a string
choices.why: Nothing secret here; both values are strings anyway.

choices.text: Tags with hyphens must be declared in quotes for Azure to inherit them
choices.why: Azure never sees the quotes; they are Bicep syntax.

choices.text: A bare property name may not contain a hyphen
choices.why: Right. `environment` is a plain name; `cost-centre` needs quotes.

prompt: The compiled `pip.bicep` shows the tags as `[union(parameters('tags'), createObject('role', 'web'))]`. When are the actual tags worked out?
hint: Who evaluates a bracketed expression?

choices.text: At compile time, by `az bicep build`
choices.why: The compiler wrote the expression and left it to be evaluated.

choices.text: When Resource Manager receives the template
choices.why: Right, with whatever value the deployment passes for `tags`.

choices.text: The first time somebody reads the resource
choices.why: Tags are fixed when the resource is created, from the evaluated expression.

choices.text: Never: Azure stores the expression as the tag
choices.why: The expression is evaluated; a tag is a plain value.

prompt: Match each of the shop's tags to the question it answers.
hint: Each tag earns its place with one question.

pairs.right: can it be switched off at night?
who do we ask before deleting it?
which product is it part of?

prompt: What does the built-in policy *Inherit a tag from the resource group if missing* do to a resource that already has the tag with a different value?
hint: Read the end of its name.

choices.text: Overwrites it with the group's value
choices.why: That is the sibling definition, which adds or replaces.

choices.text: Refuses the request until the values match
choices.why: Its effect is `modify`, not `deny`.

choices.text: Adds a second tag with the group's value
choices.why: A resource has one value per tag name.

choices.text: Leaves it as it is
choices.why: Right. It adds the tag only where it is missing.

prompt: The policy's `roleDefinitionIds` names Contributor. Why does a policy need a role at all?
hint: What does `modify` do to a resource?

choices.text: To read the group's tags, which are secret
choices.why: Tags are not secret. The role is for writing.

choices.text: Every policy definition must name a role
choices.why: Only those whose effect changes resources do; a `deny` needs none.

choices.text: Writing a tag onto a resource needs an identity allowed to write
choices.why: Right. The assignment's own identity must be given that role.

choices.text: So that the people it applies to become Contributors
choices.why: The role is for the policy's identity, not for anybody else.

prompt: The policy is assigned today. What happens to the 200 untagged machines created last year?
hint: When does a policy act?

choices.text: They are tagged within 24 hours
choices.why: Nothing happens to them by itself; the policy acts on requests.

choices.text: Nothing, until a remediation task runs
choices.why: Right. Remediation applies the modification to what already exists.

choices.text: They are tagged the next time anyone reads them
choices.why: A read is not a request to create or change.

choices.text: They are deleted for being out of line
choices.why: No policy effect deletes resources.

prompt: A shop wants its cost reports by cost centre, and does not want templates and a policy fighting over the tags on its resources. Its billing account is a Microsoft Customer Agreement. Which tool fits?
hint: One of the two changes the resources.

choices.text: Cost Management's tag inheritance
choices.why: Right. It tags the usage records only, and that agreement supports it.

choices.text: The policy with the add-or-replace effect
choices.why: That one writes on the resources, and overwrites what templates set: the fight it wants to avoid.

choices.text: Tagging only the resource groups
choices.why: Group tags do not reach the resources' usage on their own.

choices.text: Nothing: cost centres need one subscription each
choices.why: Subscriptions divide by environment; tags divide by owner, inside them.

prompt: A policy whose effect is `___` changes a request on its way in, such as adding a tag.
hint: The effect in the transcript.

prompt: Why are resource groups themselves untouched by this policy?
hint: Read the `mode`.

choices.text: A group cannot hold tags
choices.why: Groups do take tags; the shop's groups carry them.

choices.text: The policy is assigned at the scope of a resource group
choices.why: It was assigned at the subscription.

choices.text: `Indexed` mode looks only at resources with tags and a location
choices.why: Right. Groups fall outside it.

choices.text: A group would inherit from itself in a loop
choices.why: The mode excludes it before any such question arises.

prompt: In an export, which column carries the resource's tags?
hint: One JSON object in one field.

choices.text: `x_ResourceGroupName`
choices.why: That names the group, not its tags.

choices.text: `ResourceId`
choices.why: The id says where; tags say whose.

choices.text: `ChargeCategory`
choices.why: That says what kind of charge a line is.

choices.text: `Tags`
choices.why: Right, as one JSON object per line.

prompt: A program reads a daily export by opening one file in the folder. What does the lesson warn it may be missing?
hint: What happens to a large month?

choices.text: The rest of the month, partitioned into other files
choices.why: Right. Partitioning cannot be switched off.

choices.text: Yesterday's costs, which a daily export deletes
choices.why: A daily export overwrites with the month to date, yesterday included.

choices.text: The tags, which are only in Parquet files
choices.why: Tags are a column in CSV and Parquet alike.

choices.text: Amortised costs, which need a separate subscription
choices.why: Amortised cost is a dataset choice, or a column in FOCUS.

prompt: In the invented month, `who_spent.py` by actual cost put the checkout team's `cc-410` at 0.00. Why?
hint: Look at the reservation's lines.

choices.text: The machine was switched off in October
choices.why: It ran every day: its effective cost is 3.20 a day.

choices.text: Its usage was covered by a purchase, billed on an untagged line
choices.why: Right. Billed cost zero on the machine, the whole year on the purchase.

choices.text: `who_spent.py` drops lines it cannot attribute
choices.why: It counts them as `(untagged)`, never drops them.

choices.text: The tag was misspelt in the export
choices.why: It reads `cost-centre: cc-410`, exactly the scheme.

prompt: With the groups' tags lent to the resources, 139.50 stayed untagged: one resource at 4.50 a day. For how many days?
hint: October.

prompt: Billed, the invented month totals 1622.77; amortised, 553.97. A manager asks which is October's cost. What is the answer?
hint: What does the difference consist of?

choices.text: 1622.77, because that is what was invoiced
choices.why: It is what was charged, and most of it pays for months after October.

choices.text: The average of the two
choices.why: An average of two definitions is neither.

choices.text: 553.97 consumed; the rest is reservation for later months
choices.why: Right. Say which number you give, and why.

choices.text: Neither: the data is invented
choices.why: They are invented, and the question is the same for real data.

prompt: Put the three runs of `who_spent.py` in the order the lesson made them, from least to most useful.
hint: Each run fixes one thing the previous one got wrong.
items: by billed cost, with the reservation on an untagged line
by effective cost, with the reservation spread over its usage
by effective cost, with the groups' tags lent to untagged resources
trap: Inheritance comes last: lending tags does not help while the reservation sits on a line with no group at all.

prompt: After inheritance, only `vpng-shop-hub` is untagged. What should the shop do with that result?
hint: What does the leftover list name?

choices.text: Drop the line from the report as noise
choices.why: Dropping it makes the report add up to less than the bill.

choices.text: Find who owns `rg-shop-hub` and tag the group
choices.why: Right. The leftover is a list of groups nobody owns.

choices.text: Split it evenly between the two cost centres
choices.why: That decides an owner by arithmetic instead of finding one.

choices.text: Delete the VPN gateway, since nobody owns it
choices.why: Unowned in the report is not unused; it carries the office's traffic.

prompt: Which of these put a cost centre on a cost line? Choose all that apply.
hint: Think of where the tag ends up in each case.

choices.text: A tag written in the template that creates the resource
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The *if missing* policy, for resources created after its assignment
choices.why: Right, on the resource itself.

choices.text: Cost Management's tag inheritance, where the billing account supports it
choices.why: Right, on the usage records only.

choices.text: Tagging the resource group and doing nothing else
choices.why: Group tags stay on the group.

choices.text: Naming the resource group after the cost centre
choices.why: A name is not a tag, and reports do not read it as one.
